$fxv#0.displayName: T1610 - Privileged Pod Created by Non-System Principal
$fxv#0.description: A pod was created with securityContext.privileged=true by a principal outside the AKS system controller set. A privileged container holds all capabilities and effectively unrestricted host access — the most direct route to node compromise (MITRE T1610).

$fxv#10.displayName: T1098 - Client Certificate Signed and Self-Approved
$fxv#10.description: A CertificateSigningRequest was created and approved by the same principal, yielding a client certificate that authenticates to the API server independently of Entra ID. Certificate credentials survive token revocation, making this a durable persistence mechanism (MITRE T1098).

$fxv#12.displayName: T1611 - Container Escape Indicators in Container Logs
$fxv#12.description: Container stdout/stderr matched strings associated with escape tooling and techniques (nsenter, release_agent, core_pattern). BACKSTOP rule: log-string matching is evadable and sits behind the Falco syscall rule for the same technique (MITRE T1611).

$fxv#14.displayName: T1496 - Crypto Mining Indicators in Container Logs
$fxv#14.description: Container stdout/stderr matched miner binary names, mining-pool protocol strings, or known pool hostnames. BACKSTOP rule: signature matching misses renamed or novel miners and sits behind the Falco process rule for the same technique (MITRE T1496).

$fxv#16.displayName: T1550.001 - ServiceAccount Token Used Across Namespaces
$fxv#16.description: A ServiceAccount token was used to act on resources outside its own namespace, consistent with reuse of a stolen credential to pivot (MITRE T1550.001).

$fxv#18.description: Cross-namespace pod-to-pod network flows that fall outside the baseline, consistent with in-cluster service discovery or pivoting (MITRE T1046).

$fxv#2.displayName: T1611 - Pod Mounted a Sensitive hostPath Volume
$fxv#2.description: A pod was created mounting a hostPath volume that exposes the node filesystem. Mounting paths such as / or /var/run/docker.sock lets a container read or modify host state and escape its isolation boundary (MITRE T1611).

$fxv#4.displayName: T1611 - RBAC Grant for nodes/proxy Subresource
$fxv#4.description: An RBAC rule granting access to the nodes/proxy subresource was created. That subresource reaches the kubelet API directly, bypassing the API server's admission and audit controls and allowing command execution on the node (MITRE T1611).

$fxv#6.displayName: T1552.007 - Bulk Secret Enumeration via Container API
$fxv#6.description: A principal listed or read Kubernetes Secrets at a rate or scope consistent with harvesting rather than normal application access. Secrets commonly hold registry credentials, cloud tokens, and database passwords (MITRE T1552.007).

$fxv#8.displayName: T1098 - ServiceAccount Token Minted via TokenRequest API
$fxv#8.description: A principal minted a ServiceAccount token through the TokenRequest API. This is the supported way to obtain a credential for an identity other than one's own, and is a common persistence and privilege-escalation step (MITRE T1098).
